newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Southpac says IPCL offer for W&H fair.
newsitem.headline: Southpac says IPCL offer for W&H fair.

text.p: Southpac Corporation Ltd said on Thursday in its report on Independent Newspapers Plc's takeover offer for Wilson & Horton shares that the offer of NZ$10.50 per ordinary share was fair.
Southpac said IPCL's cash offer was within Southpac's assessed value range of $10.20 to $11.10 per ordinary Wilson and Horton share. It concluded the offer price was fair.
Southpac also said that the Exchangeable Shares offer was fair for shareholders who attribute full value to imputation credits.
* W&H's publishing assets between $57.9 million and $64.2 million.

The total value Southpac placed on Wilson and Horton's operating divisions was between $1.25 billion and $1.34 billion, with other assets amounting to $36.9 million and corporate overheads of between $18.9 million and $20.4 million to be deducted.
Southpac said its appraisal of the offer had been based on a share value ex the 15 cent per share 1996 interim dividend.
Southpac said it valued Wilson and Horton's main assets as follows:
* The New Zealand Herald newspaper between NZ$911.2 million and $961.2 million.
* W&H's regional newspapers between $174.4 million and $196.2 million.
* W&H's printing asets between $106.7 million and $121.7 million.

Southpac said it valued the offer based on forecasts of: an Earnings Before Depreciation, Interest and Tax multiple of between 11.2 and 12.0 for 1996 and between 9.2 and 9.8 for 1997; an Earnings Before Interest and Tax multiple of between 14.1 and 15.1 for 1996 and between 11.0 and 11.8 for 1997; and a price/earnings multiple of between 22.7 and 24.8 for 1996 and between 16.1 and 17.6 for 1997.
Southpac said it also took the following into consideration:
* There was a high level of recent trading in Wilson and Horton shares between relatively sophisticated investors at or below the IPCL offer price.
* It was unlikely there would be a competing offer.
* There was potential for a short to medium term decline in the Wilson and Horton share price if the offer was withdrawn.

Southpac said it had not considered the possible impact of New Zealand's October 12 general election or the potential value gains from further rationalisation and re-organisation which may occur in the future but which were not planned or quantified at this stage.
Southpac said its assessed value of the Exchangeable Shares alternative was up to NZ$11.47 per ordinary Wilson and Horton share.
Independent Newspapers Plc (INP) launched a takeover bid for Wilson and Horton last month through its wholly-owned subsidiary Independent Press Communications (IPCL).
INP already holds 22.6 percent of Wilson and Horton, with the same amount held by family trusts linked to INP principal Tony O'Reilly.
